title: Accessible performance of Euripides' tragedy The Trojan Women at Ancient Theater of Epidaurus
description: The National Theatre of Greece staged Euripides' tragedy The Trojan Women at the Ancient Theater of Epidaurus, Greece, on Sunday, Aug. 2, 2026. The production featured a cast of 22, including disabled and non-disabled performers, and aimed to renew global fascination with Homer's story of the Trojan War. The performance was the first fully accessible one in the ancient theater's 2,300-year history, offering accessibility services such as Braille programs, tactile models, and live audio description for blind audience members, and overhead titles for deaf spectators.

title: Yaakov Raskin | The ancient horn calling us to return
description: At the foot of the Blue Mountains is the Charles Town Maroon Museum, which showcases the history and culture of Jamaica’s Maroons. One of the museum’s unique artifacts is the abeng, a hollowed-out cow horn that is blown from the side. Historically, the abeng was used as a way to transmit coded messages which only Maroon communities could understand. Different patterns of notes transmitted various messages across long distances, including calls for communal gathering, announcements that someone had passed, or assembling search parties.
